problem_text:
A logistics company is selecting packages to load onto a cargo plane. Available shipments are:
* Package 1: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue $232
* Package 2: volume 12 cubic meters, revenue $29
* Package 3: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $279
* Package 4: volume 12 cubic meters, revenue $92
* Package 5: volume 28 cubic meters, revenue $111
* Package 6: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue $282
* Package 7: volume 38 cubic meters, revenue $36
* Package 8: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue $127
* Package 9: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue $199
* Package 10: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue $242
* Package 11: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue $154
* Package 12: volume 18 cubic meters, revenue $278
* Package 13: volume 22 cubic meters, revenue $201
* Package 14: volume 9 cubic meters, revenue $44
* Package 15: volume 42 cubic meters, revenue $235
* Package 16: volume 35 cubic meters, revenue $68
* Package 17: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue $59
* Package 18: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $94
* Package 19: volume 22 cubic meters, revenue $222
* Package 20: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $285
* Package 21: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue $190
* Package 22: volume 41 cubic meters, revenue $191
* Package 23: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue $269
* Package 24: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue $15

The aircraft has a maximum cargo capacity of 409 cubic meters. Choose the set of packages that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each package must be either fully accepted or rejected.
